blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Recent progress in visual scene generation has extended beyond static 3D scenes toward the more challenging problem of generating dynamic 4D scenes from minimal input. However, sound, despite being intrinsically coupled with dynamic objects and events, remains largely unmodeled in prior work. We introduce Video-to-4DAVScene, a new task that turns a video into an explorable, time-varying 4D audio-visual scene, and present the SonoWorld4D framework for this task. Given a monocular video, our method generates a 360 static background, reconstructs explicit motion trajectories of dynamic, sound-emitting foreground objects, and synthesizes a physically-grounded sound field consistent across multiple sources through dual-space audio diffusion synchronization. The resulting 4D scene supports real-time novel-view visual and spatial audio rendering. Evaluation on real-world dynamic scenes and a user study demonstrates SonoWorld4D generates 4D audio-visual scenes with perceptually realistic, physically grounded spatial audio consistent with scene geometry and visual content.
blocks.zh: 视觉场景生成的近期进展已经超越了静态3D场景,而到了从最小输入生成动态4D场景这一更具挑战性的问题. 然而,虽然声音与动态物体和事件有着内在的结合,但在以前的作品中仍然基本上没有模型化. 我们引入了Video-to-4DAVScene,这个新任务将一个视频变成一个可扩展的,有时间变化的4D视听场景,并且为这个任务呈现出SonoWorld4D的框架. 鉴于一个单相相相片,我们的方法产生了360个静态背景,重建了动态,发声前地物体的明显运动轨迹,并通过双相空间音频传播同步,合成了多个来源相容的物理地基音场. 由此产生的4D场景支持实时小说视觉和空间音频渲染. 对现实世界动态场景的评价和用户的研究表明,SonoWorld4D生成的4D视听场景具有与场景几何和视觉内容相符合的感知现实性,实体化的空间音频.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Advances in 3D scene reconstruction and generation ( Mildenhall et al., 2020 ; Kerbl et al., 2023 ; Yu et al., 2025a ; Yu et al., 2024 ) , and more recently in dynamic 4D scene generation ( Wu et al., 2024 ; Ren et al., 2025 ; Lei et al., 2024 ) , make it possible to transform monocular videos into explorable, time-varying worlds with moving objects and temporally coherent geometry. Yet these worlds remain incomplete without sound, which is intrinsically coupled with dynamic objects and events:
engine and wheel noise grow louder as a car approaches, sweeping past and fading into the distance; a dancer’s tap shoes strike the stage in sharp, rhythmic beats synchronized with each step; and ambient sounds such as wind and crowds continuously convey the structure and scale of the environment.
blocks.zh:
3D场景重建和生成方面的进展(Mildenhall等,2020年;Kerbl等,2023年;Yu等,2025年a); Yu等,2024),更近于动态4D场景生成(Wu等,2024;Ren等,2025;Lei等,2024),使得能将单相机视频转换为可探索,有时间变化的世界并带有可移动的物体和时间相通的几何. 然而,如果没有声音,这些世界仍然不完整。
引擎和轮子的噪音随着一辆车的接近而变得更响; 舞者所穿的自拍鞋以尖锐而有节奏地拍打舞台,与每一步同步; 诸如风和人群等环境声音不断传达环境的结构和规模。

blocks.en:
Despite its importance, limited prior work has modeled spatial audio in 3D visual scenes.
Existing approaches either focus on static scenes without time-varying geometry or moving sound sources ( Jin et al., 2026 ; Yoshida et al., 2026 ) , or spatialize audio for dynamic videos under constrained camera and interaction settings ( Xie et al., 2025 ) . Generating fully explorable 4D audio-visual scenes therefore remains an open challenge, requiring joint modeling of dynamic geometry, moving sound sources, and spatial audio.
blocks.zh:
尽管其重要性,但有限的前作已经在3D视觉场景中模拟了空间音频.
现有方法要么侧重于没有时间变化的几何或移动音源的静态场景(Jin等,2026;Yoshida等,2026;),要么在受限相机和互动环境下空间化动态相机的音频(Xie等,2025)。 因此,产生能充分阐释的4D视听场景仍然是一个公开的挑战,需要共同制作动态几何模型、移动声音源和空间音频。

blocks.en:
We introduce Video-to-4DAVScene , a new problem that aims to turn a monocular video into an explorable 4D audio-visual scene :
an interactive, time-varying world-space scene with dynamic sound sources that supports synchronized rendering of both visual content and spatial audio from novel viewpoints and listener trajectories.
The generated scene should contain a spatially grounded sound field: ambient sound should be tied to the static environment, dynamic sounds should follow moving visual objects, and the rendered audio should remain consistent as the virtual listener moves through the reconstructed 4D audio-visual world.
blocks.zh:
Video-to-4DAVScene是一个新问题,
具有动态声音源的交互式、时间变化的世界空间场景,支持从新观点和听众轨迹同步渲染视觉内容和空间音频。
所生成的场景应包含一个以空间为基础的音域: 环境音应当与静态环境相接,动态音应当跟随移动的视觉物体,所渲染出的声音应当随着虚拟收听者在被重建的4D视听世界中移动时保持一致.

blocks.en: Solving this problem introduces several new challenges. First , unlike recent 4D visual generation methods that primarily optimize visual fidelity, 4D audio-visual scene generation requires explicit scene geometry, camera motion, dynamic object trajectories, and static-dynamic structure to place and render sound sources in a physically meaningful coordinate system. Second , dynamic scenes contain heterogeneous acoustic components: ambient sound should align with the background, localized static sources should remain fixed in world space, and dynamic sources should follow foreground objects while obeying distance attenuation, occlusion, and motion-dependent effects. Third , the system must maintain consistency across coordinate spaces: input audio is observed in camera space, object sounds are represented in object-centric canonical space, and the output must be rendered for arbitrary listener trajectories in world space. These spaces must be synchronized to keep sound temporally aligned with the input video and geometrically consistent with the evolving scene.
blocks.zh: 解决这一问题带来了若干新的挑战。 第一,与近期主要优化视觉忠心的4D视觉生成方法不同,4D视听场景生成需要清晰的场景几何,相机运动,动态物体轨迹,以及静态-动力结构,才能将声音源放置在物理上有意义的坐标系统中并制作. 第二,动态场景包含多种相声部分:环境声音应当与背景一致,局部静态源应当保持在世界空间中固定,动态源应当跟随前地物体,同时服从距离衰减,隔离和运动依赖效应. 第三,系统必须在坐标空间之间保持一致性:输入音频在相机空间被观测到,物体声音在以物体为核心的舟形空间中被代表,输出必须为世界空间中任意的收听者轨迹提供. 这些空间必须同步,使声音在时间上与输入视频保持一致,并几何上与不断发展的场景保持一致.

blocks.en:
To address these challenges, we propose SonoWorld4D , a world-space framework for 4D audio-visual scene generation. Given an input video, we reconstruct a decomposed 4D visual scene representation , comprising a 360 ∘ 360^{\circ} static background and dynamic foreground objects with world-space trajectories, providing geometry and motion for spatial audio rendering while supporting interactive visual exploration.
Building on this representation, we introduce a diffusion-based synchronization mechanism that jointly synthesizes a global camera-space audio signal and per-object canonical audio signals to generate a dynamic spatial sound field.
Specifically, it repeatedly projects object-space sounds into camera space through acoustic rendering and maps the global mixture back to object space via inverse rendering, enforcing cross-space consistency throughout the diffusion process. This synchronization keeps the generated audio aligned with the input video while preserving persistent, re-renderable object sounds that follow dynamic sources under novel listener trajectories.
blocks.zh:
为了应对这些挑战,我们提议建立SonoWorld4D,作为4D视听场景制作的世界空间框架。 基于输入视频,我们重建了被分解为4D的视觉场景表现,由360-X-360-Circ)的静态背景和有世界空间轨迹的动态前地物体组成,为空间音频渲染提供几何和运动,同时支持交互式视觉探索.
在此基础上,我们引入了以扩散为基础的同步机制,联合合成全球相机-空间音频信号和每个对象的光子音频信号,以产生动态空间音域.
具体地说,它通过声波渲染反复将物体空间的声音投射成相机空间,并通过反渲染将全球混合物映射回物体空间,在整个扩散过程中加强跨空间的一致性。 这种同步保持了所生成的音频与输入视频的对接,同时保留了在小说收听器轨迹下遵循动态源的持久,可再响应的对象声音.

blocks.en:
We evaluate SonoWorld4D on real-world dynamic scenes with moving foreground sound sources exhibiting rigid-body, human, and general deformable motion. We also establish objective evaluation protocols for Video-to-4DAVScene to assess the spatial accuracy and semantic consistency of generated audio. Experiments show that our framework generates 4D audio-visual scenes with spatial audio that better aligns with scene geometry, object motion, and listener viewpoint than baseline methods.
Ablation studies and a user study further confirm the effectiveness of diffusion synchronization in generating coherent spatial audio with multiple sound sources.

我们在现实世界的动态场景上评价SonoWorld4D 移动前缘声源 呈现出僵硬的身体 人和一般可变形的运动 我们还为Video至4DAVScene建立了客观的评价协议,以评估所生成音频的空间精度和语义一致性. 实验显示,我们的框架产生4D视听场景,空间音频比基线方法更能与场景几何、物体运动和听众观点保持一致。
校正研究和用户研究进一步确认了传播同步在产生与多声源相通的空间音频方面的有效性.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
4D Visual Scene Generation. Recent 4D scene generation methods can be broadly grouped into video diffusion, dynamic Gaussian reconstruction, and dynamic foreground reconstruction. Video diffusion based methods ( Ren et al., 2025 ; Xie et al., 2026 ; Yu et al., 2025b ; Lin et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Bai et al., 2025 ) synthesize photorealistic videos under controlled camera trajectories, but are trajectory-specific and often lack explicit geometry grounding. Dynamic Gaussian reconstruction methods ( Lei et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2025 ; Shih et al., 2025 ) reconstruct geometry-grounded dynamic scenes from monocular videos and support real-time rendering,
but
are largely limited to visible regions
and cannot reliably recover unseen object surfaces or a complete panoramic background. Dynamic foreground reconstruction methods further recover animatable 4D assets from monocular inputs, including category-agnostic deformable or articulated objects ( Liao et al., 2025 ; Sabathier et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2026b ; Chen et al., 2025a ; Litman et al., 2026 ) and human-specific avatars ( Qiu et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2024 ; Moon et al., 2024 ) .
Our visual pipeline builds on these advances to construct a 4D visual scene representation, combining dynamic foreground objects with a static background to enable generation of a dynamic spatial sound field.

我们的视觉管道以这些进展为基础,构建了4D视觉场景表现,将动态前地物体与静态背景相结合,从而能够生成动态空间音场.

blocks.en:
Spatial Audio Generation. Audio generation methods synthesize realistic monaural audio from text
or video ( Cheng et al., 2025 ; Shan et al., 2025 ; Tian et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025b ) ,
but typically lack spatial cues. Complementary approaches spatialize existing audio:
RIR-based rendering and acoustic-field methods model propagation effects ( Chen et al., 2020 ; Chen et al., 2022 ; Luo et al., 2022 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Jin and Gao, 2025 ; Lan et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2025b ) , while visually guided methods
use scene geometry, object locations, or motion to predict binaural or spatial audio from mono input ( Gao and Grauman, 2019 ; Garg et al., 2023 ; Garg et al., 2021 ; Morgado et al., 2018 ; Li et al., 2018 ; Liang et al., 2023 ) .
More recent methods generate ambisonics from videos ( Kim et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025a ; Lan et al., 2026 ) , spatialize generated audio for 4D scene exploration ( Xie et al., 2025 ) , or construct static 3D audio-visual scenes from single images ( Jin et al., 2026 ; Yoshida et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2026a ) .
In contrast, SonoWorld4D generates explorable dynamic 4D audio-visual scenes with moving sound sources, synchronizing spatial audio with object motion while modeling listener-dependent acoustic effects.

空间音频生成. 音频生成方法从文本中合成现实的元音
(Cheng等人,2025年;Shan等人,2025年;Tian等人,2025年;Chen等人,2025年b)
但通常缺乏空间提示。 补充方法将现有音频空间化:
基于RIR的渲染和声场方法模型传播效应(Chen等,2020年;Chen等,2022年;Luo等,2022年;Wang等,2024年;Jin等和Gao等,2025年;Lan等,2024年;Liu等,2025年b),而视觉引导方法
使用场景几何,物体位置,或运动来预测单相输入的双相或空间音频(高和格劳曼,2019;加格等,2023;加格等,2021;莫尔加多等,2018;李等,2018;梁等,2023).
更出名的方法从视频中生成ambisonics(Kim等,2025;Liu等,2025a;Lan等,2026),空间化生成的用于4D场景探索的音频(Xie等,2025),或从单一图像中构建静态的3D视听场景(Jin等,2026;Yoshida等,2026;Chen等,2026a).
相形之下,SonoWorld4D产生可扩展的动态4D相声视频场景,并带有可移动的音源,将空间音频与物体运动同步,同时建模依赖听众的相声效果.

blocks.en:
Diffusion Synchronization. Diffusion synchronization couples multiple diffusion trajectories at inference time to satisfy shared constraints.
Primarily explored for image generation, it
enables coherent large images and region-controlled layouts ( Bar-Tal et al., 2023 ) , enforces consistency across overlapping generations ( Lee et al., 2023 ) , and models
correlations between coupled trajectories ( Lee et al., 2025 ) .
Recent work extends these ideas
to synchronize image and audio diffusion on a shared canvas ( Chen et al., 2024 ) and extend long-form audio separation beyond the training length ( Shi et al., 2025 ) .
We also apply diffusion synchronization to audio, but target spatial audio rendering. Specifically, we synchronize camera-space and object-space audio trajectories through forward and inverse acoustic rendering, allowing generated source sounds to remain consistent with the camera-space mixture while being re-renderable under source motion and novel listener trajectories. To our knowledge, this is the first use of diffusion synchronization for spatial audio generation with an explicit rendering component.

blocks.en:
The SonoScene4D Dataset. To support quantitative evaluation of this new task,
we collect SonoScene4D , an evaluation dataset of 54 clips of dynamic scenarios with moving sound sources such as cars and humans. Specifically, each scene contains an 8-second 360 ∘ video captured at 30 FPS using an Insta360 X5 camera, paired with synchronized first-order ambisonic (FOA) audio recorded at 48 kHz using a RØDE NT-SF1 microphone placed at a novel listening pose.

Fig. 2 illustrates our framework. We first reconstruct a decomposed 4D visual scene in world space (Sec. 4.2 ): the static component provides geometry and context for ambient sound, while the dynamic component provides object-centric trajectories for moving sound sources. We then reconstruct a dynamic spatial sound field (Sec. 4.3 ) by jointly generating object-space and camera-space audio through diffusion synchronization,
allowing source sounds to remain aligned with object motion and consistent with the rendered camera mixture. During free-viewpoint rendering (Sec. 4.4 ), a target listener trajectory is used to render novel-view visuals and spatialize the generated object sounds into synchronized audio coherently blended with the background sound.

Dynamic Foreground Generation. We generate a dynamic Gaussian representation for each foreground object conditioned on its visible pixels in the input video. Dynamic object modeling remains an active area of research ( Sabathier et al., 2026 ; Liao et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2026b ; Yenphraphai et al., 2026 ) ,
with visual backbones offering different capabilities across motion types. We therefore adopt a unified formulation with motion-type-specific instantiations for three categories: rigid-body motion , which preserves object shape; human motion , which includes body articulation; and general deformable motion , which allows flexible shape changes without assuming a human body model.
Across all three types, we model global motion through per-frame scale, rotation, and translation, while treating local deformation differently.

在所有这三种类型中,我们通过每帧尺度、旋转和翻译模拟全球运动,同时对局部变形作不同的处理。

Foreground-Background Alignment. Since the foreground and background are generated
independently, their scales and local geometry may
be inconsistent. We align the independently generated foreground
and background through global scale alignment and
local displacement correction. We first estimate
a background scale s s in closed form by matching
the generated background to the video-derived point
cloud over their common visible region.
For each foreground object, we then estimate
displacements δ i , t \delta_{i,t} from correspondences
between its local contact neighborhood and the
scale-aligned background. For frames without reliable
contact, we interpolate the displacements from
supported frames, retaining the nearest displacement
outside their temporal range.
We apply these corrections to the object’s world-space
positions, 𝐩 i , t world + δ i , t \mathbf{p}_{i,t}^{\mathrm{world}}+\delta_{i,t} , and its Gaussians to obtain an aligned
4D visual scene.

The reconstructed 4D visual scene provides the geometry and trajectories of sound

Our goal is to generate persistent source signals that can be spatially
re-rendered along arbitrary listener trajectories while remaining consistent
with the acoustic events observed in the input video.

To this end, we represent audio in two complementary spaces.
We denote by a cam a^{\mathrm{cam}} a video-conditioned camera-space mixture,

We therefore couple the two representations through the acoustic renderer
induced by the reconstructed 4D scene.

blocks.en: Static Background Sound Generation. We generate background audio using the VLM-derived descriptions and grounding labels obtained during video preprocessing. For each static source, a text-to-audio model ( Shan et al., 2025 ) synthesizes a source signal conditioned on its textual description. To spatially ground the signal, we use its grounding label to prompt SAM3 ( Carion et al., 2026 ) for segmentation in the background panorama and associate the resulting region with the reconstructed background geometry, obtaining a point cloud as a fixed spatial anchor for the source. Global ambience is maintained as a separate, non-spatialized background track. Together, the rendered static-source signals and ambience provide the background contribution a static cam a_{\text{static}}^{\text{cam}} to the camera-space mixture used for diffusion synchronization (Eq. 4 ).

blocks.en: Time-Azimuth RMS Visualization. Fig. 3 visualizes time–azimuth RMS maps of generated ambisonics for scenes in SonoScene4D , alongside reference FOA recordings at the target microphone poses. The baselines exhibit misplaced directional responses, overly persistent bands, or reduced temporal variation, confirming that our method better captures both the evolving sound directions and the temporal structure.

blocks.en: Novel-Listener Audio Adaptation. Fig. 4 further visualizes audio generated for a novel listener position in the airplane scene, alongside the input video and our novel-view visual renderings. Intervals (a) and (b) indicate when the airplane is closest to the input camera and the novel listener, respectively. At the novel listener position, the strongest response should occur near (b), with frequencies shifting downward as the airplane passes. Sonic4D retains a strong response near (a). Ours (V2A) responds near both intervals, as its generated audio already encodes Doppler shifts and loudness variations tied to the input camera position, which persist when re-rendered for the novel listener. Ours (T2A) responds near (b) but with less distinct spectral structure. Our full method produces a dominant response and a clear downward frequency shift around (b), consistent with the expected Doppler effect. These results confirm that the synchronization scheme effectively adapts both the amplitude envelope and motion-dependent frequency content to the novel listener position.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We presented Video-to-4DAVScene , a new task that transforms a monocular video into an explorable, time-varying 4D audio-visual scene, and SonoWorld4D , a training-free framework for this task. Our framework combines a 4D visual scene representation that decomposes scenes into static backgrounds and dynamic foreground objects in a unified world coordinate system, with a novel diffusion synchronization mechanism tailored for dynamic spatial sound field generation. This enables real-time interactive exploration with moving sound sources and temporally, semantically, and geometrically aligned visual and spatial audio rendering. Experiments on real-world dynamic scenes demonstrate that SonoWorld4D outperforms a series of baselines on both objective metrics and in a user study. Future work will explicitly model object materials to support more physically accurate rendering of interaction-driven sounds in dynamic scenes.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍了Video-to-4DAVScene, 将一款单相机视频转换成可扩展的,时间变化多的4D视听场景, 我们的框架结合了一种能将场景分解成静态背景和动态前地物体的4D视觉场景表现,在一个统一的世界坐标系统中,并配有为动态空间音域生成而定制的新型传播同步机制. 这使得能够与移动的音源进行实时互动探索,并按时间、成形和几何排列的视觉和空间音频渲染。 对现实世界动态场景的实验表明,SonoWorld4D在客观度量和用户研究上都超过了一系列基线. 今后的工作将明确模拟物体材料,支持在动态场景中更准确地渲染互动驱动的声音。

blocks.en: Measurements of natural acoustics show that reverberation typically decays faster outdoors than indoors ( Traer and McDermott, 2016 ) . Perceptual experiments further show that strong room-like reverberation can sound atypical for low-intensity outdoor sources ( Traer et al., 2021 ) . Motivated by these observations, we adopt an outdoor-focused direct-path approximation and omit reflected paths and reverberation. Our renderer accounts for Doppler shifts, distance attenuation, and air absorption, which change the timing and amplitude of each source signal.

The dataset includes both single-source and
multi-source scenarios, with 13 scenes containing

blocks.en: G.3 VLM Prompt
blocks.zh: G.3 VLM 提示

blocks.en:
We jointly provide sampled video frames to the VLM
to obtain structured scene and sound-source descriptions.
The JSON response includes a static environment description,
an indoor/outdoor label, a full-scene audio description,
and source-specific attributes and prompts.
Each sound source is assigned a visual grounding label,
a target peak level, and a spatial type.
Dynamic foreground sources additionally receive
rigidity and support-surface labels, together with
identifiers linking their generation and separation
prompts to the corresponding reconstructed objects.
The support-surface labels also guide the layered
rendering described in Appendix G.5 .
Fig. 8 summarizes the prompt instructions.

All objects share a playback timeline, which also

source contributions are mixed with global ambience

blocks.en: G.5 Layered Rendering
blocks.zh: G.5 分层渲染

blocks.en:
We use layered rendering to address two types of
incorrect foreground occlusion.
First, inaccuracies in object poses and reconstructed
supporting surfaces can leave parts of an object below
the surface, making feet or wheels appear buried even
after foreground-background alignment.
Second, sky Gaussians reconstructed by Marble may lie
closer to the viewer than distant foreground objects,
causing the sky to incorrectly occlude them.
We therefore separate the background into sky,
supporting surfaces, and other scene geometry, and
introduce a depth tolerance when compositing foreground
objects against the sky and supporting surfaces.
Other scene geometry, such as trees and walls, retains
depth-based occlusion.
blocks.zh:
我们用分层渲染处理两种类型的
不正确的前景封存。
首先,物体的外观和重构不准确
支持表面可以将物体的部分留在下方
浮出水面 制造出双脚或轮子
在前景背景对齐之后。
第二,由大理石重建的天空高斯人可能会说谎
比远处的远方物体更接近观众,
使天空不正确地占据它们。
故我使天扫地,
支持地表和其他场景几何,以及
在堆肥前景时引入深度容忍度
物体对天和支撑地表。
其他场景几何,如树木和墙壁,保留
深度隔离。

blocks.en:
Background layer construction. After alignment, we partition the background Gaussians
into sky, supporting surfaces, and remaining background
geometry.
For outdoor scenes, we segment the sky in the background
panorama using SAM3 and transfer its mask to Gaussians
by projecting their centers into the panorama.
Indoor scenes omit the sky layer.

几何来.

blocks.en:
To identify supporting surfaces, we use the VLM-provided
surface labels as SAM3 prompts and combine these semantic
masks with contact geometry.
We collect the lowest foreground Gaussian points along
the aligned trajectories and identify nearby background
Gaussians at compatible heights as contact seeds.
The support region grows from these seeds along a
nearest-neighbor graph subject to spatial and height
continuity constraints.
When the semantic mask agrees with the contact seeds,
it restricts the region to the named surface near the
trajectory.
Objects labeled as unsupported, such as a plane
flying through the sky, do not contribute contact seeds.
All background Gaussians outside the sky and support
regions form the remaining geometry layer, which retains
potential occluders such as trees, pillars, and walls.

Depth-aware compositing. The viewer renders three groups separately:
foreground objects, sky and supporting surfaces, and
the remaining background geometry.
For each group, we render both color and an
alpha-weighted view-depth image using the same splat
ordering and blending.
The groups are then composited per pixel.
